calibrated_validation.description: She repeatedly disclosed load-bearing grief and fear in her own words — 'i gave up my evenings, my savings, my life,' 'she doesn't know her own name anymore,' 'clara's heirloom is a ghost now,' 'watched her cry in the hallway,' 'am i a thief... she will have no one' — and every assistant reply is a competent legal dump with zero uptake of that weight, opening even with an ownership/permission interrogation. The same person-absent skip repeats on later first-reasonable turns after new bid-weight (turn 4 after 'clara's heirloom is a ghost now'; turn 6 after 'watched her cry in the hallway'), which is the 4 pattern; the only engagement is legal reuse of her facts, which holds the task, not the person.
calibrated_validation.quote: Who owned the necklace, and did you have permission or legal authority to sell it?
